title: Hermes
subtitle: hermes-agent (OSS) + Langfuse + HITL
description: Built around Nous Research's open-source hermes-agent: a nightly eval loop in Langfuse, plus a weekly job that clusters the agent's weakest turns and proposes edits to its own prompt. It runs on a 3-node homelab with local inference, and every proposed edit waits for my approval in Telegram.

title: Inference Engine
subtitle: llama.cpp + ROCm + Local Agentic Workflows
description: Three models on one box serve every agent I run at $0 per call, which changes which experiments are worth running. It's a from-source llama.cpp build on an AMD APU the project doesn't officially support, where memory bandwidth alone should cap the dense 27B model at 7.4 tokens/sec. It doesn't. Every call is traced, and nothing sensitive leaves the LAN.

title: Pi-Cloud
subtitle: Private Infrastructure + Service Operations
description: A Raspberry Pi 5 running 22 containers — photos, passwords, document search, DNS filtering, private search, monitoring — with zero public ports and two recovery paths on different filesystems. Two of its services also back an agent that calls them unattended. An off-network audit, not the green firewall status, is what found 15 services one layer short of the isolation I intended.

title: Job-Fit Scorer
subtitle: LangGraph + FastAPI + Langfuse
description: A LangGraph pipeline that scores job postings against evidence of what I've actually built, tuned to say no as readily as yes. A cheap pre-filter drops irrelevant postings before any LLM sees them. One real week: 21 scored, 2 worth applying to, 19 skipped, with recurring blockers tallied into a study list. Every run is traced in Langfuse, and the weekly health check is deterministic rather than an LLM grading its own homework.

title: AI Chat Assistant
subtitle: Gemini 2.5 Flash + Cloudflare Workers + Structured Context
description: The assistant in the corner of this page — try it, that's the whole demo. A Cloudflare Worker feeds Gemini a compact, structured reference for the whole portfolio on every request, skipping the vector database the obvious build reaches for. It can also turn a reply into a real UI action — opening the resume, jumping to a section. One eval question caught it confidently repeating a wrong answer: not a hallucination, a bad source file.

title: myPal
subtitle: AAC App Prototype (2021, not actively maintained)
description: An AAC (picture-based communication) app for kids with autism and speech delays, built for classrooms and homes where the wifi can't be counted on. Every card and phrase lives in SQLite on the device first and syncs across iOS and Android once a connection shows up. Offline-first wasn't bolted on later; it was the constraint the rest of the app was built around.
